name: Halifax
tagline: Maritime Charm, Ocean Views, and Canada's Most Affordable Coast
description: Halifax is the cultural and economic hub of Atlantic Canada, offering a walkable waterfront downtown, a thriving food scene built on fresh seafood, and housing costs far below Toronto or Vancouver. Universal healthcare, a strong sense of community, and proximity to stunning Nova Scotian coastline make Halifax an underrated FIRE destination for those who enjoy maritime living and four-season outdoor recreation.

quickFacts.visa: No visa required for Canadian citizens. Others: Super Visa (for parents/grandparents, up to 5 years) or Visitor Record extensions. No dedicated retirement visa — Canada lacks a retiree-specific immigration pathway.
quickFacts.safetyRating: High – one of Canada's safest cities
quickFacts.climate: Humid continental with cold, snowy winters and warm summers; ocean-moderated

housing.description: Older studio or bachelor unit in Fairview, Spryfield, or Dartmouth, priced for value over polish

dining.description: Mostly home cooking, with fish-and-chips and pub nights as the regular outing

healthcare.description: MSI covers doctors and hospitals; basic dental-and-prescription extended supplement. Note: MSI requires Nova Scotia residency — a non-resident early retiree should budget for private cover

transportation.description: Halifax Transit monthly pass (C$82.50); the downtown core is walkable

entertainment.description: Free waterfront boardwalk, Point Pleasant Park, festivals, and the library

1M.lifestyle: An older studio or bachelor unit in Fairview, Spryfield, or across the harbour in Dartmouth, chosen for price over polish. Most meals are cooked at home, with a fish-and-chips outing or a pub night as the regular treat, and getting around leans on the Halifax Transit pass in a walkable downtown. Nova Scotia's MSI covers doctors and hospitals, so the health line is just basic dental-and-prescription extended cover. The free waterfront boardwalk, Point Pleasant Park, and a strong festival-and-library culture carry the leisure budget. Cold, snowy winters with short days are the main tradeoff, but the maritime setting makes a careful budget feel rich.

housing.description: Proper one-bedroom in Clayton Park, the West End, or Dartmouth

dining.description: Out a couple of times a week across the seafood-and-brewery scene

healthcare.description: MSI plus private supplemental (dental, vision, physio, prescriptions)

transportation.description: A reliable paid-off car for exploring Nova Scotia, with winter tires and insurance

entertainment.description: Theatre, live music, sailing lessons, and a gym membership

2M.lifestyle: A proper one-bedroom in Clayton Park, the West End, or Dartmouth, with dining out a couple of times a week across the seafood-and-brewery scene and a reliable car for weekend drives to Peggy's Cove or the Cabot Trail. Private supplemental cover on top of MSI keeps medical costs low, and theatre, live music, and a gym round out an unshowy, comfortable maritime routine.

housing.description: Nice modern one-bedroom in the South End, downtown, or a North End new-build

dining.description: Frequent quality dining, including fine seafood rooms like Bar Kismet and Stories

healthcare.description: MSI plus comprehensive private cover for faster access. Note: MSI requires Nova Scotia residency — a non-resident early retiree should budget for private cover

transportation.description: A late-model car, premium insurance, and harbour ferry access

entertainment.description: Sailing-club membership, cottage weekends, and the arts calendar

3M.lifestyle: A nice modern one-bedroom in the South End, downtown, or a North End new-build, with dining out several times a week across Halifax's seafood-driven food scene. A late-model car opens up the South Shore and the Cabot Trail, comprehensive private cover layers faster access on top of MSI, and sailing, cottage weekends, and the arts calendar are all within reach. This is a relaxed, financially-secure life in a walkable maritime city with real discretionary room.

housing.description: Luxury one-bedroom or junior-two-bedroom in a downtown waterfront high-rise (King's Wharf, Queen's Marque)

dining.description: Fine dining several nights a week plus private-chef occasions

healthcare.description: MSI plus executive-health and premium private supplements

transportation.description: A luxury vehicle plus regular flights from YHZ

entertainment.description: Yacht-club and golf memberships, arts patronage, private sailing

domesticHelp.description: Weekly housekeeping plus snow removal and yard care

luxuryExtras.description: A South Shore cottage, quarterly international travel, and boat access

5M.lifestyle: A luxury one-bedroom or junior-two-bedroom in a downtown waterfront high-rise, frequent fine dining, a nice car, and a weekly housekeeper. Yacht-club and golf access, cottage getaways, premium private cover, and quarterly international travel put this well into upscale territory for a city this size, with a large margin over what Halifax's cost of living requires.

housing.description: Prime luxury two-bedroom or penthouse at the top of Halifax's market

dining.description: Near-daily fine dining and catered occasions built on Atlantic seafood

healthcare.description: MSI plus concierge-grade and international medical cover. Note: MSI requires Nova Scotia residency — a non-resident early retiree should budget for private cover

transportation.description: A luxury vehicle, chartered flights, and boat access for coastal cruising

entertainment.description: Major maritime and arts philanthropy, private regattas, extensive travel

domesticHelp.description: Full domestic help — housekeeper, groundskeeper, property management

luxuryExtras.description: Multiple properties, first-class travel, a boat, and community philanthropy

10M.lifestyle: A prime luxury two-bedroom or penthouse at the top of Halifax's market, near-daily fine dining and catered occasions built on Atlantic seafood, a luxury car, chartered flights from YHZ, and boat access for coastal cruising. Full domestic help and concierge-grade private cover complete the ceiling. Halifax's luxury infrastructure is genuinely limited, so much of this tier funds travel, philanthropy, and the quiet prestige of a maritime waterfront address rather than big-city extravagance.
